gsm.ctas end to end

gsm-ctas.Rmd

gsm.ctas runs the ctas anomaly detection engine inside the gsm workflow framework, so that CTAS site scores appear alongside the usual KRIs in a standard gsm site report.

This vignette walks the whole path – SDTM domains in, rendered KRI report out – and then covers the two things most users will want to change: the thresholds, and the set of metrics.

Installation 

install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("IMPALA-Consortium/ctas")
pak::pak("Gilead-BioStats/gsm.core")
pak::pak("Gilead-BioStats/gsm.mapping")
pak::pak("Gilead-BioStats/gsm.kri")
pak::pak("Gilead-BioStats/gsm.reporting")
pak::pak("IMPALA-Consortium/gsm.ctas")
library(gsm.ctas)

The shape of the pipeline

gsm is a YAML-driven engine: each layer is a directory of workflow files, and RunWorkflows() executes them in order.

lRaw --Ingest--> lIngest --1_mappings--> lMapped --2_metrics--> lAnalysis
     --3_reporting--> Reporting_* --4_modules--> HTML report

gsm.ctas ships all four layers in inst/workflow/:

Layer Contents
1_mappings DM, VS, LB, SITE, STUDY, plus CTAS_Input -> CTAS_SiteScores -> CTAS_Detail
2_metrics ctas0001-ctas0011, one per parameter family x CTAS feature
3_reporting Groups, Metrics, Results, Bounds
4_modules report_kri_site

The important structural point: CTAS is an all-metrics-at-once engine. One ctas::process_a_study() call scores every timeseries x feature x site, so it runs once, in 1_mappings/CTAS_SiteScores.yaml, and each metric workflow merely filters the shared Mapped_CTAS_SiteScores object down to one parameter family and one feature.

Input data

pharmaversesdtm provides the SDTM domains. The example is cut down to six sites and a handful of tests to keep the engine fast.

vSites <- sort(unique(pharmaversesdtm::dm$SITEID))[1:6]

dfDM <- pharmaversesdtm::dm[pharmaversesdtm::dm$SITEID %in% vSites, ]
dfVS <- pharmaversesdtm::vs[
  pharmaversesdtm::vs$USUBJID %in% dfDM$USUBJID &
    pharmaversesdtm::vs$VSTESTCD %in% c("SYSBP", "DIABP", "PULSE"),
]
dfLB <- pharmaversesdtm::lb[
  pharmaversesdtm::lb$USUBJID %in% dfDM$USUBJID &
    pharmaversesdtm::lb$LBTESTCD %in% c("ALB", "BILI", "CREAT"),
]

lRaw <- list(
  Raw_DM = as.data.frame(dfDM),
  Raw_VS = as.data.frame(dfVS),
  Raw_LB = as.data.frame(dfLB)
)

1. Mapping and the CTAS run 

lMappingWorkflows <- workr::MakeWorkflowList(
  strNames = NULL,
  strPath = system.file("workflow/1_mappings", package = "gsm.ctas"),
  strPackage = NULL
)

lIngest <- gsm.mapping::Ingest(
  lRaw,
  gsm.mapping::CombineSpecs(lMappingWorkflows)
)

# CTAS emits `cor()` "standard deviation is zero" warnings for flat series.
# They are genuine data-quality signal, so the package does not suppress them;
# only this vignette does.
lMapped <- suppressWarnings(
  gsm.core::RunWorkflows(lWorkflows = lMappingWorkflows, lData = lIngest)
)

names(lMapped)
#> [1] "Mapped_DM"              "Mapped_LB"              "Mapped_VS"             
#> [4] "Mapped_SITE"            "Mapped_STUDY"           "Mapped_CTAS_Input"     
#> [7] "Mapped_CTAS_SiteScores" "Mapped_CTAS_Detail"

Labs are mapped twice from the same domain, because the two questions are different:

  • Input_Range() -> LB_NORM_* – do a site’s values deviate, once the reference range has made different tests comparable?
  • Input_Missing() -> LB_MISS_* – does its completeness deviate? The value-based input drops missing results, so it is structurally blind to this.

Mapped_CTAS_SiteScores is the shared result: one row per timeseries x feature x site, carrying the identifiers needed to tell the families apart.

utils::head(lMapped$Mapped_CTAS_SiteScores, 3)

#> 1  LB_MISS_ALB                 Labs        ratio_missing
#> 2  LB_MISS_ALB                 Labs        ratio_missing
#> 3  LB_MISS_ALB                 Labs        ratio_missing

unique(lMapped$Mapped_CTAS_SiteScores[
  , c("parameter_category_1", "parameter_category_3")
])
#>     parameter_category_1 parameter_category_3
#> 1                   Labs        ratio_missing
#> 109                 Labs     range_normalized
#> 253          Vital Signs              numeric

The mapping functions also work directly, outside a workflow:

lInput <- Combine_CTAS_Input(
  dfVS = Input_Numeric(
    dfDomain = lMapped$Mapped_VS,
    strSubjectCol = "USUBJID",
    strTestCDCol = "VSTESTCD",
    strTestCol = "VSTEST",
    strValueCol = "VSSTRESN",
    strVisitCol = "VISIT",
    strVisitNumCol = "VISITNUM",
    strCategory = "Vital Signs",
    strPrefix = "VS"
  ),
  dfSubjects = Input_Subjects(
    dfDM = lMapped$Mapped_DM,
    strSubjectCol = "USUBJID",
    strSiteCol = "SITEID",
    strCountryCol = "COUNTRY"
  )
)

names(lInput)
#> [1] "data"                    "subjects"               
#> [3] "parameters"              "custom_timeseries"      
#> [5] "custom_reference_groups" "untransformed"

2. Metrics

Each metric filters the shared scores to one family and one feature, then aggregates timeseries into the gsm Analysis_Analyzed contract.

lMetricWorkflows <- workr::MakeWorkflowList(
  strNames = NULL,
  strPath = system.file("workflow/2_metrics", package = "gsm.ctas"),
  strPackage = NULL
)

lAnalysis <- gsm.core::RunWorkflows(
  lWorkflows = lMetricWorkflows,
  lData = lMapped
)

The aggregation is:

gsm field CTAS source
GroupID site_scores$site
Numerator timeseries with trigger == "Further Evaluation"
Denominator timeseries evaluated for that group x feature
Metric Numerator / Denominator
Score max(fdr_corrected_pvalue_logp)

Flagging is one-sided (0/1/2): −log⁡10p-\log_{10}p is unsigned, so it says that a site differs, not in which direction.

Denominator counts timeseries, not participants and not tests – CTAS autogenerates a timeseries per timepoint combination, so the lab families contribute more of them than vital signs do.

3-4. Reporting and the KRI report

There is deliberately no Reporting_Input. CTAS has no subject-level numerator/denominator – each subject contributes a whole timeseries and the statistic is computed on a distribution – so synthesising one would be a fiction that renders misleadingly. The stock gsm.kri site report does not need one.

lModuleWorkflows <- workr::MakeWorkflowList(
  strNames = NULL,
  strPath = system.file("workflow/4_modules", package = "gsm.ctas"),
  strPackage = NULL
)

workr::RunWorkflows(lModuleWorkflows, lReporting)

The module drops the stock scatter plot via DropChart(). That chart plots Denominator against Numerator, which suits a rate metric where the denominator is exposure; here it is a coverage count, near-identical across sites, so the points collapse onto one x position. The bar chart and KRI table carry the same information on the −log⁡10p-\log_{10}p scale the metric is actually defined on.

Customising thresholds

Thresholds are exposed the gsm-native way, through meta and ParseThreshold. Edit the metric YAML – no code change, no fork:

meta:
  Threshold: 0.842, 2.326   # flagging cut points, -log10(p) scale
  TriggerHigh: 2.326        # timeseries -> "Further Evaluation"
  TriggerLow: 0.842         # timeseries -> "Watch List"

TriggerHigh / TriggerLow classify timeseries, feeding Numerator. Threshold classifies groups, feeding Flag. The same numbers, different jobs.

The defaults 2.326 and 0.842 are one-sided normal z-quantiles (99% and 80%) applied to a −log⁡10p-\log_{10}p scale, where they correspond to p≈0.0047p \approx 0.0047 and p≈0.144p \approx 0.144. They are adopted from operational experience for consistency with existing CTAS review, and documented here rather than silently inherited.

To use your own workflows, copy the shipped directory and point MakeWorkflowList() at the copy:

lMyMetrics <- workr::MakeWorkflowList(
  strNames = NULL,
  strPath = "my_workflows/2_metrics",
  strPackage = NULL
)

Adding a metric

A new metric is a YAML file, not a function. Copy ctas0001.yaml and change a few meta fields:

meta:
  ID: ctas0012
  Metric: CTAS Labs Missingness Autocorrelation
  Feature: autocorr               # a ctas timeseries feature
  Domain: "Labs"                  # parameter_category_1
  Transformation: "ratio_missing" # parameter_category_3

Domain and Transformation are required together, and Summarize_CTAS() errors if only one is supplied. Neither identifies a family alone:

Domain Transformation
VS_* Vital Signs numeric
LB_NORM_* Labs range_normalized
LB_MISS_* Labs ratio_missing

A selector matching nothing is an error rather than an empty result: zero timeseries would render every site as unevaluated, which is indistinguishable from a genuinely absent domain.

To score a feature the shipped workflows do not compute, add it to Features in 1_mappings/CTAS_SiteScores.yaml as well.

Drill-down: handing off to ctasapp

Aggregation collapses many timeseries into one row per site. The timeseries detail is retained separately for the ctasapp dashboard, which is the tool for investigating a signal that the gsm report has detected.

lDetail <- lMapped$Mapped_CTAS_Detail
vapply(lDetail, nrow, numeric(1))
#>       Results         Input Untransformed 
#>           324         14053         14053

Results is the site scores unchanged; Input is the analysed series joined to site and parameter labels; Untransformed holds the original values, so a lab result can be shown in its own units next to the range-normalised value that was actually analysed. Write them out for upload with:

Write_CTAS_Detail(lDetail, strPath = "ctas_detail", strFormat = "csv")

parquet is available via Suggests: arrow, and is worth using for deployment – Input is one row per subject x parameter x timepoint and grows quickly.
